description: A 'Q proof' graphic on a black background titled 'Q PROOF:' with the closing banner 'PROOFS ARE IMPORTANT - Q'. It juxtaposes screenshots of Q drops #628 and #634 (Jan 27 2018), which mention John Perry Barlow and state 'Heart attacks can be deadly', with a Heavy.com article and a Wikipedia excerpt reporting Barlow's death on February 7, 2018 in San Francisco. The graphic implies Q foreknowledge of Barlow's death; Barlow had a documented 2015 heart attack and died in his sleep, and the implied causal connection is an unverified claim.

Updated Feb 7, 2018 at 6:53pm. 1. The Cause of Death Was Not Immediately Clear but Barlow Had Health Problems in Recent Years. How John Perry Barlow died was not immediately clear, but his health had not been good in recent years. In 2015, a heart attack led to other health issues and saddled Barlow with heavy medical bills. He wrote about the heart attack on social media, saying, "I was dead for about 8 minutes on Wed eve. Total cardiac arrest. Hard to relax & sleep now. And sad to report no Ascending Light.". WIKIPEDIA The Free Encyclopedia. John Perry Barlow. Death [edit]. Barlow died in his sleep on the night of February 7, 2018 at his San Francisco home, at the age of 70.[103][104][105]. description: Screenshot of Q drop #1945 (tripcode !!mG7VJxZNCI, 28 Aug 2018) as rendered by a Q aggregator app, headed 'QAnon Censorship on Microsoft Xbox Live (Proof)'. The drop attaches an image combining an Xbox Live outage-tracker dashboard and outage map with screenshots of two earlier Q drops (Aug 15-16 2018) mentioning 'PS/Xbox chat logs', annotated 'DO YOU BELIEVE IN COINCIDENCE?' and 'JUST AFTER Q POSTS XBOX GOES DOWN'. The drop links a r/greatawakening Reddit thread claiming QAnon content was deemed hate speech. The implied connection between the Q posts and the Xbox Live outage is the graphic's claim, not an established fact.

description: Screenshot of Q drop #1906 (tripcode !!mG7VJxZNCI, Aug 16 2018), which replies '>>2627990' to a quoted Anonymous 8chan post. The anon post embeds a screenshot of a GamesBeat/PC Gaming article by Jeff Grubb, 'Xbox Live is down, so how will teens yell at me now?' (Aug 15 2018), reporting a Microsoft-confirmed Xbox Live outage, shown with a flaming Xbox Live logo image and sidebar ads for Lincoln and Chevrolet. The anon cites two post numbers 'for anyone questioning if this happened or not'. The screenshot documents the outage article; any implied link between Q posts and the outage is the thread's claim.
